objectives.text: Keep the state alive against one of its own entities. The objective of the state-level institutions (the Bosniak-led majority in the Presidency and the Council of Ministers' Troika coalition, the Constitutional Court, the State Court, the Central Election Commission) is to defend the Dayton order, territorial integrity and the writ of state justice against the Republika Srpska leadership, which after Dodik's 26 Feb 2025 conviction banned the state judiciary and police from the entity (the OHR said this 'hint[s] at de facto secession') and now asks for the army, border police, intelligence and fiscal system back. These are not the objectives of the Serb member of the Presidency or of the HDZ BiH leadership (see reading).

grand_strategy.reading:
Bosnia and Herzegovina has no single grand strategy, and a card that pretends it
has one would be wrong. The objectives above are those of the state-level
institutions as the Bosniak-led majority reads them: the Presidency member
Becirovic, the foreign minister Konakovic, the Constitutional and State Courts,
the Central Election Commission, the SDA/SDP/Troika parties. Two other agendas
sit inside the same state. The Republika Srpska leadership of Dodik's SNSD,
which has just won again, wants to hollow the state out - competences back to
the entity, the OHR gone, status defined in Washington and Moscow - and keeps
the Serb seat in the Presidency (Cvijanovic) to veto what it cannot win. The
HDZ BiH leadership of Covic, backed by Zagreb, wants an election law that stops
non-Croats from choosing the Croat member and has just obtained the seat
outright. The paradox of the whole card is that a state must defend its
existence against one of its own entities, with tools (the Bonn powers, EUFOR,
Security Council cover, the courts) that belong in part to others, in a year in
which the guarantors weakened - Schmidt resigned in May and no successor was
agreed by mid-July, the US lifted its sanctions and said it was done with
nation-building, Orban fell in April - while the electorate stayed home (42%).
Signals that are not rows: the 31 Oct 2026 Security Council vote on EUFOR (the
October 2025 renewal was 15-0, so the base case is renewal; Russia's line on the
OHR is the thing to watch), the identity of the next High Representative,
whether Hungary under Magyar keeps Orban's line toward Banja Luka, and whether
the new Presidency can still produce a majority on foreign-policy questions
after Komsic's seat goes to HDZ. Sarajevo's room for manoeuvre is real only
where the EU and the entity cannot veto it: the courts, memory politics and the
capacity to say no to Belgrade.

stances.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded rival - Republika Srpska is an entity of the state (own territory in law); the actor graded here is its leadership, which competes with the state. Territorial grades apply to territories, not actors. As Sarajevo's state institutions see it: Republika Srpska is an entity of the state, within the territorial integrity the Security Council reaffirmed on 29 Dec 2025, but its leadership has banned state judiciary and police (27 Feb 2025, annulled by the Constitutional Court), keeps its own police and budget, and demands the army, border police, intelligence and fiscal system back. Claimed, not fully controlled: the state did execute the Dodik verdict and the entity repealed the laws on 18 Oct 2025 under pressure, so 'own_territory' is the alternative reading. Not 'adversary': the state does not seek the entity's end, and the entity's leadership formally invokes Dayton. No source uses the grade word (confidence C). Cooling because SNSD won again on 4 Oct 2026 and US sanctions were lifted. Bond grievance: the 1992-95 war and the entity's origin. Serbia grades RS 'ally', so the pair SRB-RS is deliberate. Mirrors the evidence in SRB's stance toward sub-rs and XKX's toward sub-rs.

relations_to.summary: Dodik was sentenced by the State Court to one year in prison and a six-year ban for defying the High Representative (26 Feb 2025); the next day the RS National Assembly passed laws banning the State Court, prosecutors and police from the entity (and a foreign-agents law). The Constitutional Court suspended them on 7 Mar 2025 and annulled them on 29 May 2025; an appeals court upheld the verdict on 1 Aug 2025. Mirrors the state's own row.

relations_to.summary: On 12 Aug 2025 the State Court replaced Dodik's one-year prison term with a fine of about EUR 18,660 at the defence's request, leaving the six-year ban in place. The Central Election Commission had already stripped him of the RS presidency (6 Aug 2025, after the final verdict), the Constitutional Court rejected his appeal in November, and on 18 Oct 2025 the Assembly installed Ana Trisic-Babic as acting president and repealed the annulled laws. No plea agreement with the State Prosecutor's Office was found in any source.
relations_to.note: The brief's plea-deal element could not be verified: searches in English and Bosnian returned nothing. A pardon by the state Presidency (three-member consensus, prior opinion of the State Court) was being debated in Bosnian media in October 2026; no pardon has been granted.

relations_to.summary: Early RS presidential election on 23 Nov 2025 won narrowly by Sinisa Karan (SNSD, about 50.3% to 48.4% for Branko Blanusa on a turnout of about 35%); the CEC annulled 136 polling stations on 24 Dec 2025 and in the rerun of 8 Feb 2026 Karan again beat Blanusa. Dodik, barred from office, ran the campaign. Mirrors the state's own row.

relations_to.summary: In the general elections of 4 Oct 2026 SNSD kept the entity (Savo Minic elected RS president, about 202,000 votes to 161,000), Zeljka Cvijanovic (SNSD) won a second term in the state Presidency with about 55%, and overall turnout fell to about 42%, a record low. Dodik declared victory 'at all levels' and said he would not change course. Mirrors the state's own row.
relations_to.note: Preliminary results; the CEC had not certified the final count when checked.

relations_to.summary: In April 2025 High Representative Schmidt suspended public funding to SNSD and its coalition partner after the conviction, a Bonn-powers decision Germany publicly backed; Schmidt then announced his resignation on 10-11 May 2026, the Peace Implementation Council failed on 4 June and 30 June to agree a successor (the US backed Antonio Zanardi Landi, France, the UK and Germany Rene Troccaz), and US diplomat Louis Crishock became acting High Representative on 1 July 2026. No permanent successor was confirmed in any source reached.
